analysis: The PR changes only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md: it bumps the "Last updated" date (line 3) and adds a sentence at around line 170 saying a lifecycle drain on a provider with no registered session completes without a graceful-drain acknowledgement once accepted work and local response writes finish (`ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift`, `performLifecycleDrain`). The supplied units are unchanged base text at lines 579-1229, which gave context for the protocol surface (models_replace, drain, cache receipts, inference_request, and the attestation and code_attestation challenges). The doc edit alters no code, wire format, or security control. The documented behavior is that, with no registered session, there is no coordinator connection to acknowledge a drain on. Pending work still finishes before the drain completes, so no inference cancellation or data-exposure path is evident. The existing text still states that a dead connection cannot deliver a graceful-drain acknowledgement, and the models_replace requirement that `drain_request_id` name a committed and settled drain on the exact live connection (lines 919-921) is unaffected. Threat entries T-053 and T-057 are not weakened by the documentation. Open question for integration: the head-side Swift implementation of `performLifecycleDrain` is not supplied. It should be checked that the no-session drain path cannot be used to satisfy the model-switch drain precondition (prepareModelSwitch returning a drain ID) without a coordinator-settled drain, and that admission stays closed after the drain. This is an unverified code contract, not a finding. No threat-model update is needed from this documentation-only change.
